SOURCE EXTRACT — read from the full djvu texts, 2026-09-06
=========================================================
YEAR BOOK AND OFFICIAL ROSTER OF THE YMCAs OF NORTH AMERICA — the volumes for 1891 and 1892
Internet Archive: ymcayearbookof1891younuoft, ymcayearbookof1892younuoft

NEITHER IS LENDING-RESTRICTED. Both djvu texts downloaded whole (672,945 and 630,720 bytes) and
searched. "Kanawana" occurs ZERO times in either, as in all twelve volumes of this series now read.

These two were taken last and are the most important of the series for this project, because they
cover the year of the Jones' Island trip (1891) and the autumn the camp committee was appointed
(1892).


===============================================================================
1. THE 1892 VOLUME — W. H. BALL, JR. CAME FROM SPRINGFIELD, AND A CONTEMPORARY
   PRINTED SOURCE SAYS SO
===============================================================================

From the QUEBEC provincial narrative report, signed at its foot "CHARLES CUSHING, Cor. Mem.":

    "QUEBEC.
    The Quebec Association is at present without a general secretary. The Association at Sherbrooke,
    under its new secretary, is doing an active and earnest work. The membership of the Montreal
    Association has reached 1,600, and the new building has the appearance of an African ant hill,
    swarming with workers in every department, and severely taxing the energies of the general
    secretary and his assistants. The religious meetings continue large and impressive, and bear
    much fruit. THE PHYSICAL DIRECTOR, W. H. BALL, JR., A NEW MAN, FROM THE SPRINGFIELD TRAINING
    SCHOOL, IS DOING EXCELLENT WORK; the classes for pastors and business men, as well as those for
    young men and boys, are all thronged, and the great plunge and the shower baths are new and
    exceedingly popular features of the building. In the canvass for subscriptions for the new
    building the International Committee rendered very valuable and opportune assistance in the
    personal services of Secretary Claus Olandt, Jr., for which the Montreal Association is deeply
    grateful.
                                                            CHARLES CUSHING, Cor. Mem."

    (The OCR gives "CHARLES GUSHING" and "Glaus Olandt"; both are read as C.)

And the same volume's roster:

    "Montreal — D. A. Budge. Asst., D. W. Corbett. PHYS. DIRECTOR, W. H. BALL, JR."


WHY THIS IS THE FIND
--------------------
`billy-ball.md`'s Open Question 5 asks whether the Montreal "Billy" Ball is **William Henry Ball,
Springfield College class of 1891**, who graduated alongside James Naismith and Amos Alonzo Stagg
and later ran the YMCA's national swimming campaign. The article's answer has been "**strongly
corroborated, not fully proven**", and the KB's own `f_1245` states the objection precisely:

    "His known career positions (Yonkers, Brooklyn, Springfield, Detroit, then YMCA International
    Committee 1911-1924) DO NOT INCLUDE MONTREAL, but a Montreal posting between 1891 and his other
    documented positions has not been ruled out."

Here is a contemporary printed source, published by the YMCA's own International Committee, saying
that Montreal's physical director W. H. Ball, Jr. was **a new man from the Springfield Training
School**. The Springfield man graduated in 1891; the Montreal man is new in the volume for 1892.

**This does not prove the two are one man.** It does something more useful than another name match:
it removes the only structural objection there was. The Springfield-to-Montreal path is now
documented from the Canadian end, by a source with no interest in the question, written by the
Quebec corresponding member who would go on to chair the Permanent Camp Committee.

The proof that would close it is still the Springfield College finding aid MS 527, which is
JavaScript-rendered and inaccessible to this environment, or a direct enquiry to that archive.


===============================================================================
2. THE 1891 VOLUME — THE POST WAS EMPTY THE YEAR BEFORE
===============================================================================

    "QUEBEC.
     Montreal — D. A. Budge. Asst., W. J. Orr. Asst., Percy C. Leslie.
     Quebec — F. W. Gooch.
     Sherbrooke — D. C. Stephens."

**No physical director at all.** Which is what "a new man" in the next volume means, and which fits
this project's record of Ball as Physical Director from September 1891 — after this volume was
compiled and before the next.


===============================================================================
3. AND R. L. CHARLTON, WHOM THE NAME SWEEP COULD NOT FIND
===============================================================================
The 1891 volume prints the provincial committee:

    "ONTARIO AND QUEBEC. Appointed February, 1891. Headquarters, Toronto, Ont.
     C. S. Gzowski, Jr., Toronto, Ont., Chairman. J. O. Anderson, Secretary.
     John J. Gartshore, Treasurer.
     [Toronto members] … Herbert Ames, Montreal, Que. — D. A. BUDGE — R. L. CHARLTON —
     George Hague — R. Henderson — R. H. Holland — F. W. Kelly …"

**R. L. Charlton sat on the Ontario and Quebec Provincial Committee, appointed February 1891** —
three years before he appears on the 1894 Summer Camp committee that founded Kanawana, and seven
before the 1898 Camp Jubilee photograph. He is in Montreal company: Herbert Ames, the reformer who
wrote *The City Below the Hill*, and George Hague, the banker.

This project's name sweep ran "R. L. Charlton" against a full-text index of millions of books on
2026-09-06 and got thirteen hits, none of them him. He was in a volume of a series already sitting
in this repo's cache. **That is rule 21 for the third time in one day.**


===============================================================================
THE SERIES, AS IT NOW STANDS
===============================================================================
TWELVE volumes read for the Montreal roster: 1891, 1892, 1893, 1894, 1895, 1896, 1897, 1906, 1907,
1908, 1921, 1922. STILL UNREAD: the four Google scans (1882, 1886, 1896, 1907, 1921 — duplicates of
years already held, but worth checking for different printings) and the 1936 volume, which may be
restricted. See p_433.
